work.title: Implement variance() and stdev() in calc with unit tests
work.result: Implemented population variance() using mean() and stdev() as its square root; both support generators and raise ValueError on empty input. Added known-value, single-element, empty-input, and generator tests. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: Ran 7 tests in 0.000s, OK. Committed on main as 050d60782b0c320fb778ed2c8eb994216aaab1e2 (Add population variance and standard deviation). No push. Git identity was absent, so used the existing repository commit identity hubdemo <hubdemo@localhost> for this commit only.

work.title: Review variance()/stdev() implementation in calc (commit 050d607)
work.result: APPROVE: commit 050d607 meets the requirements. variance() is the population variance (sum of squared deviations divided by N; [1,2,3,4] is 1.25, not the sample 5/3). stdev() is variance(xs) ** 0.5 on the same materialized sequence. Both raise ValueError on []. Both list(xs) first, are plain functions, and variance() reuses mean(). Tests cover the population value, stdev, a single element (0), empty input for both functions, and generators. unittest: 7 tests, OK. Extra checks (floats, negatives, zeros, two elements, all-equal, generator consumed once) match the population definition. Non-blocking: stdev([]) reports "variance of empty sequence" because it delegates to variance(); the required ValueError is still raised.
